disabled.description: The bundled charts k3s is told not to install. Replaces the package's own list rather than adding to it. The components k3s 1.37 packages are offered as suggestions, not as the whole vocabulary: a chart the engine bundles without advertising it under --disable is accepted too, and cargoship warns when it configures a node with a name this build does not package.

chart.description: The Helm chart this package carries and the helm controller installs. Turning it off again uninstalls the release: the HelmChart resource owns it, and cargoship prunes the manifest a disabled chart wrote.

enabled.description: Whether the cluster installs the charts this package carries -- all of them; the gate is per package, not per chart. Off in the package, because a chart an example carries to demonstrate the mechanism is not something a cluster should get for having installed the example.

addressPool.description: The addresses the cloud provider hands to Services of type LoadBalancer, as a CIDR or a start-end range. Must be free, routable on the nodes' own subnet, and outside whatever DHCP hands out - a package ships a documentation-range default that works nowhere, because it cannot know a cluster's spare addresses. It must also exclude spec.config.loadbalancer: a pool holding the control-plane VIP eventually hands it to a Service, and kube-vip answers for it on whichever node won that Service, taking the API server down intermittently.

interface.description: The interface kube-vip adds Service addresses to. Empty lets it take the host's default-gateway interface, which is what makes one value correct across nodes whose NICs are not named alike.

usernames.description: Users whose pods skip pod security admission entirely. Replaces the package's list rather than adding to it.

runtimeClasses.description: Runtime classes whose pods skip pod security admission entirely. Replaces the package's list rather than adding to it.

namespaces.description: Namespaces whose pods skip pod security admission entirely. Replaces the package's list rather than adding to it, so name kube-system and zarf as well or the cluster's own components are enforced against.
